✅ Risk Score: LOW (10/100)

2 Medium

Review completed with 2 findings across 1 agents (2 medium).

findings.title: Relaxed type safety for `SupportsItems` may hide incompatible objects
findings.description: The previous `SupportsItems` protocol used non-restrictive generic typing `Iterable[tuple[Any, Any]]` for its return type. Changing this to `SupportsItems[_KT_co, _VT_co]` where `Any` is no longer the default return type for methods might cause `dict.items()` and similar implementations to be incompatible with strict type checkers unless the methods explicitly define their types, potentially hiding real injection/data handling issues during refactoring.
findings.suggestion: Review the codebase to ensure that every object passed to `dict_to_sequence` or `to_key_val_list` implements the `SupportsItems` protocol correctly with the expected key/value types. Ensure that when objects are passed into these functions, they strictly adhere to the new generic constraints. Add a regression test that verifies that passing a custom object with an incompatible `.items()` type causes a type error, ensuring that untyped/dangerous objects are not silently accepted.

findings.title: Broadening `KVDataType` to `SupportsItems[Any, Any]` may accept non-standard iterable objects
findings.description: The type alias `KVDataType` was updated to replace `Mapping[Any, Any]` with `SupportsItems[Any, Any]`. While this increases flexibility, passing a `dict` directly to `to_key_val_list` will now be caught by the type checker if the dict's values are not fully generic (e.g., `dict[str, int]` instead of `dict[KT, VT]`). This can lead to runtime errors if `to_key_val_list` expects to call `dict.items()` but receives a custom `SupportsItems` object that raises exceptions or returns data in an unexpected format.
findings.suggestion: Ensure that `to_key_val_list` performs strict runtime type checking and exception handling on the `value` parameter when it is a `SupportsItems` object, not just a standard `Mapping` or `Iterable`. Wrap the call to `value.items()` in a `try-except` block to handle `TypeError` or `AttributeError` securely and reject invalid data early rather than allowing a malformed object to reach downstream serialization or query building logic.
